newsitem.title: UK: Europe cross-border fund activity up sharply - study.
newsitem.headline: Europe cross-border fund activity up sharply - study.

text.p: European funds have targeted Germany as the best country in which to market their products amid a sharp rise in cross-border fund activity in Europe over the past two years, a study by Lipper Analytical said.
The study showed a surge in registration of UCITS -- European funds authorised to market their product across Europe -- with 2,939 now registered against 1,174 in 1994.

"The principal market for true cross-border UCITS is Germany. International investment fund groups have identified Germany as the European market with the richest potential pickings," the report said.
It said the UK, Austria, France and the Netherlands were also popular markets.

Lipper said the number of "true cross-border" UCITS, defined as those which are sold in two or more markets other than their home market, had tripled in the past two years and by mid-1996 had assets of $290.7 billion.

The concept of UCITS was introduced in 1985 to establish a framework where fund management groups in one EU state could market its product to investors in other countries, provided they meet local marketing requirements.
It covers all 16 EU member states, Dublin, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway.
Of some 3,000 foreign UCITS, three-quarters are based in Luxembourg, with Dublin the second most important base.
It said Flemings was the most internationally minded player, with registrations in 13 countries and 33 true cross-border funds.
It is followed by Fidelity and Banque Indosuez.
